# Content gates

<!-- This file is generated by `npm run gates:docs` from packages/gates/src/docs/gates.template.md and the rule
registry. Do not edit it by hand: a unit test fails when it is out of date. -->

Every content pull request (a passage, a translation, a calendar year, corpus or config) passes five gates before it
can merge. Each gate is a named, self-explaining test: every finding it reports names a rule, says what must hold and
how to fix it. The gates never close a PR. A failure blocks it until the author pushes a fix, and anything uncertain
waits for a person.

- The rules: [decision 003](decisions/003-auto-merge.md) (auto-merge threshold and human approval).
- The reviewer's side: [reviewer guide](reviewer-guide.md).
- The code: [`packages/gates`](../packages/gates/src/registry.ts); the workflows:
  [content-checks.yml](../.github/workflows/content-checks.yml) and
  [content-gates.yml](../.github/workflows/content-gates.yml).

## The five gates

They run in this order: the cheap deterministic gates first, then the verifiers, then the merge rule.

| #   | Gate                        | Kind                   | Rules | What it checks                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --- | --------------------------- | ---------------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Schema tests (`schema`)     | deterministic          | 20    | Every changed passage, translation and calendar file is valid, well keyed and fully cited: each sentence ends in a claim marker, each claim names a source, nothing is orphaned and approvals are well formed.              |
| 2   | Evidence tests (`evidence`) | deterministic          | 4     | The cited evidence exists: web excerpts are found on the fetched page, scripture excerpts and original-language words occur in the corpus at that verse. Print sources cannot be checked, so they are flagged for a person. |
| 3   | Licence guard (`licence`)   | deterministic          | 6     | No long verbatim run from an English Bible or a cited commentary: quoted spans, overlap with the public-domain Bible index, overlap with each fetched web source and excerpt length all have limits.                        |
| 4   | LLM verifiers (`verifiers`) | LLM, trusted side only | 8     | Two models from different families see only the claims and their sources: the confirmer checks support, the refuter tries to refute. Each gives a verdict and a support score per claim.                                    |
| 5   | Merge rule (`merge-rule`)   | decision               | 22    | Reads the other gates’ results, the config and the facts of the PR (approvals, approval commits, paths, fork) and decides one of the decisions below. It never closes a PR.                                                 |

## How a content PR is checked

Two workflows share the work. The split exists because a `pull_request` run executes the copy of the workflow that
the PR itself carries, so it must hold nothing worth taking.

```text
content-checks.yml (pull_request: opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled; read-only, no secrets)
  changes → deterministic (schema, evidence, licence)
        │ workflow_run (completed)
        ▼
content-gates.yml (always main's copy; the only workflow with a write token or the verifier keys)
  resolve → gates-trusted → verifiers → decide → merge
        ▲                                (decide → approve → upload artifact → dispatch)
        │ issue_comment (/approve), workflow_dispatch on main
```

**content-checks.yml, the PR side.** It has `contents: read` and no secrets. `changes` decides whether anything the
gates read changed (`passages/`, `calendar/`, `corpus/`, `config/`); if not, the gates exit green. A changed symbolic
link or submodule fails `changes`. `deterministic` runs schema, evidence and licence with the live source fetcher (SSRF
guard on) and writes the gates table to the job summary. Its required checks are `changes` and `deterministic`.

**content-gates.yml, the trusted side.** It starts when content checks complete, when someone comments on a PR (only
`/approve` comments do anything), or by dispatch on main. Every trigger runs main's copy of the file; a dispatch off
main does nothing.

1. `resolve` re-reads the PR and its head from GitHub. Nothing the PR-side run produced is used.
2. `gates-trusted` runs schema, evidence and licence again.
3. `verifiers` runs the two LLM verifiers, in the `llm-verifiers` environment (below). It runs only on a new head that
   is not an approval commit, and never for a fork PR.
4. `decide` runs the merge rule in three phases. **decide** gathers the PR facts, decides, sets the decision label and
   updates the one sticky gates comment. **approve** (only for `human-approved` or `auto-merge`) writes the review
   block and one approval commit; the workflow then uploads the artifact `lectio-approval-pr<n>-<commit sha>`.
   **dispatch** runs every required-check workflow on the approval commit (commits made with the workflow token
   trigger nothing by themselves) and publishes the `merge-rule` check run on the PR head.
5. `merge` runs on `approved-commit`: it waits for every required check on the approval commit, squash-merges with
   `--match-head-commit`, then dispatches the deploy.

The full report (every result, the head and the decision) is uploaded as the `gates-report` artifact. Download it
when the comment says findings were left out for its size.

### Threat model and trust boundaries

- **Nothing from the PR side is trusted.** `resolve` finds the PR from GitHub (the PRs listed for the completed run, or
  the open PR whose head is the run's head sha) and checks that the head is still the PR's head. The deterministic
  gates run again on the trusted side.
- **Base-checkout rule.** Every job checks out main at the commit `resolve` saw and runs `npm ci` there. The PR head is
  fetched only as data into `pr-head/`: files are read as regular-file git blobs, and the PR's `package.json`,
  lockfile and scripts are never installed or run. A PR that edits `decide` or a gate cannot change its own decision.
  The config, the gate registry and the Prettier config all come from main.
- **Least privilege per job.** Permissions default to none. `resolve` and `gates-trusted` read; `verifiers` reads and
  is the only job with secrets; `decide` and `merge` write. Checkouts never persist the token.
- **Approval commits.** The commit's trailer `Lectio-Approval: <human|auto> run=<id> head=<sha>` names the run that
  wrote it. It counts only if that run executed main's copy of content-gates.yml and uploaded the artifact naming this
  PR and this exact commit sha, the commit is authored by `github-actions[bot]` with a verified signature, and the
  trailer's head is the commit's parent. Anything else with that trailer is forged and the PR is `blocked`. The merge
  uses `--match-head-commit` on that sha. Run titles are never trusted.
- **Hand-set review blocks.** A PR that sets a review block to approved without a counted approval or a valid
  approval commit is `blocked`: only the merge-rule job writes approvals.
- **Fork PRs** are report-only: a red `merge-rule` check and the job summary; no labels, comments, commits or
  verifiers. A maintainer merges them by hand.
- **PRs that change `.github/**`** get no approval commit, no dispatch and no merge from the workflow (a
  `pull_request` run executes the PR's own copy of content-checks.yml). A maintainer merges them by hand after
  approval.
- **Protected paths.** A PR that changes `packages/gates/**`, `.github/**`, `config/**` always needs a person, whatever the scores.
  This is code, not config, so it cannot be switched off from config.
- **Revoking.** Removing the label or deleting the comment after the approval commit was written does not stop the
  merge job. To stop it, close the PR or push to it.

## The merge rule

`decide` checks, in order: a failed deterministic gate (`blocked`); an approval commit at the head (`approved-commit`,
or `blocked` when forged); a hand-set review block (`blocked`); a counted human approval (`human-approved`); any review
condition (`needs-review`); otherwise `auto-merge`.

| Decision          | `merge-rule` check | Label                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `approved-commit` | green              | `auto-merge-candidate` | The head is a valid approval commit written by the merge-rule job. The `merge` job waits for every required check on it and squash-merges.                                                                         |
| `blocked`         | red                | `gates-failed`         | A deterministic gate failed, a changed file is a symbolic link or submodule, an approval commit is forged, or the PR sets a review block to approved by hand. Nothing merges until the author pushes a fix.        |
| `human-approved`  | green              | `auto-merge-candidate` | A configured reviewer added the approval label or commented the approval command after the last content commit. The job writes the review block in an approval commit, which is then decided as `approved-commit`. |
| `auto-merge`      | green              | `auto-merge-candidate` | Every gate passed and both verifiers support every claim at `autoMerge.minSupport` or higher, with no refutation and no review condition. The job writes an `auto` review block in an approval commit.             |
| `needs-review`    | red                | `needs-review`         | Anything else: a flag, low support, a refutation, a sensitive claim, a skipped verifier, a protected path, a translation, a fork PR, files outside `passages/`. The PR waits for a person; it is never closed.     |

The job keeps exactly one of `auto-merge-candidate`, `needs-review`, `gates-failed` on the PR.
A green decision on a PR that must be merged by hand (it changes `.github/**`) gets `needs-review`.

### Approving

A person approves a PR in one of two ways:

- add the **`approved` label** (the config's `reviewer.approvalLabel`), or
- comment **`/approve`** (`reviewer.approvalCommand`) as the first line of a new comment.

It counts only when the actor is in `reviewer.githubHandles` and the approval came after the last content commit; a
new content commit resets it. For the label, the latest time the label was added counts and removing it revokes it.
An edited comment never counts, because anyone with write access can edit a comment. **The PR author may approve**:
the research CLI opens PRs under the owner's account, and GitHub does not let an author approve their own PR review,
so the label and the comment avoid that limit. The merge-rule job then writes the review block (`method: human`,
`approvedVia: label` or `comment`) in an approval commit and merges. The [reviewer guide](reviewer-guide.md) walks
through it.

### Config

The merge rule and the licence guard read these keys from `config/lectio.config.json`; the defaults are:

| Key                                      | Default        |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `autoMerge.enabled`                      | `true`         |
| `autoMerge.minSupport`                   | `0.9`          |
| `autoMerge.requireBothVerifiers`         | `true`         |
| `autoMerge.maxRefutations`               | `0`            |
| `autoMerge.sensitiveClaimsRequireReview` | `true`         |
| `autoMerge.flagsRequireReview`           | `true`         |
| `autoMerge.passagesOnly`                 | `true`         |
| `reviewer.githubHandles`                 | `["nyabongo"]` |
| `reviewer.weeklyCapacity`                | `15`           |
| `reviewer.maxOpenReviewPrs`              | `15`           |
| `reviewer.approvalLabel`                 | `"approved"`   |
| `reviewer.approvalCommand`               | `"/approve"`   |
| `licenceGuard.maxQuotedWords`            | `10`           |
| `licenceGuard.maxExcerptWords`           | `25`           |
| `licenceGuard.maxCommentaryRunWords`     | `12`           |
| `licenceGuard.maxBibleRunWords`          | `12`           |
| `licenceGuard.shingleSize`               | `8`            |

`config/` is a protected path, so changing a threshold always needs a person.

## The `llm-verifiers` environment

The two verifier keys, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`, live as secrets of the GitHub environment
`llm-verifiers`, which only protected branches (main) can deploy to. The `verifiers` job is the only job that runs in
it, so no other job, and no PR-side run, can read the keys. `scripts/repo/setup.sh` creates the environment; the owner
moves the keys into it by hand and deletes any repository-level copies. Without both keys the verifiers gate is
skipped, and a skipped verifier means `needs-review`.

## Required checks

Branch protection on main requires every job listed in [`.github/required-checks/`](../.github/required-checks/), plus
`merge-rule`: a check run the `decide` job publishes through the Checks API, so it is not a workflow job and not in
the registry. Every required check is pinned to the GitHub Actions app, so a check of the same name from any other
source does not count. `scripts/repo/setup.sh` builds the protection from the registry (owner only; `--dry-run` prints
the calls), and `npm run required-checks` validates the registry. The rules for required-check workflows are in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md#workflows-and-required-checks).

## Rules by gate

Every finding names one of these rules. The PR comment repeats the rule and its fix under each finding.

### 1. Schema tests (`schema`)

- **`schema/valid-passage`**: Every passages/<key>.json file is valid JSON and matches the passage schema (@lectio/schema/passage).
  - Fix: Correct the field named in the message; docs/content-model.md lists every passage field and its shape.
- **`schema/valid-calendar`**: Every calendar/<year>.json file is valid JSON, matches the calendar-year schema, and lists its days in date order inside its year.
  - Fix: Correct the field named in the message, or rebuild the year with `npm run calendar:build`.
- **`schema/key-matches-filename`**: A passage file is named after its `key`, and a calendar file after its `year`.
  - Fix: Rename the file to passages/<key>.json (or calendar/<year>.json), or correct `key` / `year` inside it.
- **`schema/ref-parses`**: Every reference parses: the passage `key` is canonical, `ref` parses to that key, and every scripture source and calendar reading `ref` parses.
  - Fix: Write the reference as the lectionary prints it (`Mt 20:1-16a`) and the key as `toKey` writes it (`MT.20.1-16`, ADR 0004).
- **`schema/ref-is-real-verse`**: Every reference names verses that exist (original/NABRE versification, @lectio/refs L-006).
  - Fix: Check the chapter and verse numbers against a Bible; Psalms use the Hebrew numbering.
- **`schema/note-verse-in-passage`**: Every translation note’s `verse` falls inside the passage its file covers.
  - Fix: Correct the note’s `verse` (`chapter:verse`), or move the note to the passage that contains that verse.
- **`schema/claim-has-source`**: Every claim cites at least one source, and every id in its `sourceIds` names a source in the same file.
  - Fix: Add the supporting source to `sources[]`, or correct the id in the claim’s `sourceIds`.
- **`schema/source-is-cited`**: Nothing is orphaned: every source is used by a claim, and every claim is cited by a `[cN]` marker in the text.
  - Fix: Remove the unused source or claim, or cite it where the text relies on it.
- **`schema/sentence-cites-claim`**: Every sentence of every context paragraph and translation-note body ends with at least one `[cN]` marker naming a claim in the same file.
  - Fix: Add the marker of the claim that supports the sentence (`… a day’s wage. [c9]`), or add that claim; correct markers that name no claim.
- **`schema/unique-ids`**: Ids are unique: claim, translation-note and source ids within a passage; dates within a calendar year; celebration and Mass ids within a day.
  - Fix: Rename or merge the duplicate; never renumber ids that are already published (see schema/note-ids-stable).
- **`schema/note-ids-stable`**: Every translation-note id and claim id on the base branch still exists after the change, because insight permalinks point at them.
  - Fix: Restore the removed or renamed id; add new notes and claims with new ids instead of reusing or renumbering old ones.
- **`schema/approved-has-reviewer`**: An approved passage records a valid approval: a human approval by configured reviewers via cli, label or comment, or an auto approval whose verifier summary meets the auto-merge thresholds.
  - Fix: Set `review` back to `{ "status": "pending", "reviewers": [] }` and approve through `npm run review:approve`, the approval label or the approval comment.
- **`schema/no-fake-provenance`**: Content made by the fake generator never lands: `provenance.generator` is not `fake` and no model is `fake`.
  - Fix: Regenerate the passage with the research CLI and real providers (or mark a hand-written seed as `manual-seed`).
- **`schema/calendar-keys-wellformed`**: Every calendar reading’s `key` is a canonical passage key and equals the key of its `ref`.
  - Fix: Rebuild the year with `npm run calendar:build`, or set the reading’s `key` to the key `toKey(parseRef(ref))` gives.
- **`schema/valid-translation`**: Every passages/i18n/<locale>/<key>.json file is valid JSON and matches the translated-passage schema (@lectio/schema/translated-passage).
  - Fix: Correct the field named in the message; a translation carries only the localised summary, context, note texts and claim texts, with the English ids.
- **`schema/translation-of-exists`**: A translation sits at passages/i18n/<locale>/<translationOf>.json, with `locale` naming its directory, and the English passage passages/<translationOf>.json exists and is valid.
  - Fix: Move or rename the file to match `locale` and `translationOf`, or add (or restore) the English passage it translates; delete translations of a removed passage.
- **`schema/translation-matches-source`**: A translation lines up with its English passage: the same translation-note and claim ids, the same number of context paragraphs, and the same `[cN]` markers in each paragraph and note body.
  - Fix: Translate every note and claim of the English file under its English id, keep the paragraphs one for one, and copy each claim marker to the matching place.
- **`schema/translation-not-stale`**: A translation’s `sourceSha256` equals the hash of the English passage’s translatable fields, so it says what the English says now.
  - Fix: Re-run `npm run research -- translate --locale <locale> --only <key>` (or update the translation by hand and set `sourceSha256` to translatableSha256 of the English file).
- **`schema/translation-quoted-run`**: A quoted span in a translation is at most licenceGuard.maxQuotedWords words long (the licence guard’s quoted-run limit, applied to the translated text).
  - Fix: Quote a single word or a short phrase, or say it in your own words; a Bible translation in any language is linked out, never quoted at length.
- **`schema/translation-needs-review`**: Translations never auto-merge: every pending translation in a pull request waits for a person.
  - Fix: Ask a configured reviewer to read the translation and approve it (`npm run review:approve`, the approval label or the approval comment).

### 2. Evidence tests (`evidence`)

- **`evidence/web-excerpt-found`**: Every web source’s excerpt appears in the page fetched from its URL (a page that cannot be fetched is flagged for review).
  - Fix: Copy the excerpt word for word from the page at the source URL (or its archivedUrl), or correct the URL. If the page is gone, add an archivedUrl.
- **`evidence/scripture-source-real`**: Every scripture source cites real verses, and its Greek, Hebrew, Aramaic or Latin excerpt occurs in those verses of the corpus. An excerpt containing Greek or Hebrew script is checked as Greek or Hebrew whatever its excerptLang says (even `en`), and must be tagged grc, hbo or arc.
  - Fix: Correct the source’s ref to the verse it quotes, or copy the excerpt from that verse of the original text.
- **`evidence/original-word-in-verse`**: Every word a translation note quotes in the original language occurs in that verse of the corpus edition for its language.
  - Fix: Correct the note’s verse, or spell original.text as it stands in that verse (SBLGNT or LXX for Greek, OSHB for Hebrew and Aramaic, the Vulgate for Latin).
- **`evidence/print-source-flag`**: A claim resting on a print source cannot be checked automatically, so it is flagged for a reviewer.
  - Fix: A reviewer checks the citation against the book. Where possible, also cite a web or scripture source the gate can check.

### 3. Licence guard (`licence`)

- **`licence/quoted-english-run`**: A quoted English span in a passage note is at most licenceGuard.maxQuotedWords words long.
  - Fix: Quote a single word or a short phrase, or say it in your own words; the reading itself is linked out, never quoted at length.
- **`licence/pd-bible-overlap`**: No note text shares a run of licenceGuard.maxBibleRunWords or more words with a public-domain English Bible (World English Bible, Douay-Rheims).
  - Fix: Rewrite the sentence in your own words and point to the verse by reference instead of reproducing its wording.
- **`licence/commentary-overlap`**: No note text shares a run of more than licenceGuard.maxCommentaryRunWords words with the fetched text of a cited web source.
  - Fix: Paraphrase the commentary in your own words; keep the source in sources[] and, if needed, a short excerpt.
- **`licence/commentary-unchecked`**: Every cited web source can be fetched and read, so the note can be checked against it.
  - Fix: Fix the URL or add an archivedUrl that loads; otherwise a reviewer must compare the note with the source by hand.
- **`licence/excerpt-length`**: A source excerpt is at most licenceGuard.maxExcerptWords words long.
  - Fix: Trim the excerpt to the few words that support the claim.
- **`licence/guard-index`**: The public-domain shingle index loads and matches the configured shingle size and the textguard normaliser version, and licenceGuard.maxBibleRunWords is at least the shingle size.
  - Fix: Rebuild the index with `npm run guard:build` (packages/textguard) and commit corpus/guard/ together, or fix licenceGuard in config.

### 4. LLM verifiers (`verifiers`)

- **`verifiers/two-families`**: The confirmer and the refuter come from two different model families, each as configured.
  - Fix: Set config.verifiers.confirmer and .refuter to different families, and inject live clients of those families.
- **`verifiers/live-verifiers`**: With config.verifiers.mode "live", both verifiers are live clients.
  - Fix: Provide the confirmer and refuter API keys to the content-gates job, or set config.verifiers.mode to "auto".
- **`verifiers/passage-readable`**: A changed passage file parses and validates, so its claims can be verified.
  - Fix: Fix the problems gate 1 (schema) reports for the file; the verifiers then check its claims.
- **`verifiers/claim-not-refuted`**: Neither verifier refutes a claim.
  - Fix: Correct or remove the claim, or cite a source that supports it as written; a person settles disagreements.
- **`verifiers/verifier-answered`**: Both verifiers return a well-formed verdict for every claim.
  - Fix: Re-run the gates; if the provider keeps failing or answering malformed output, a person reviews the claims.
- **`verifiers/claim-supported`**: Both verifiers judge every claim supported, with support at or above config.autoMerge.minSupport.
  - Fix: Cite a source (with an excerpt) that states the claim directly, or narrow the claim to what the sources say.
- **`verifiers/claim-not-sensitive`**: A claim either verifier flags as doctrinally or pastorally sensitive waits for a person.
  - Fix: A reviewer reads the claim and its sources and approves the PR if it is sound.
- **`verifiers/live-results`**: Verifier results count as evidence only when they come from live models; a fake run always waits for a person.
  - Fix: Nothing to fix in content: the verifiers ran on fake clients (config.verifiers.mode "fake"), so no verifierSummary is recorded.

### 5. Merge rule (`merge-rule`)

- **`merge-rule/deterministic-gates-pass`**: The deterministic gates (schema, evidence, licence) must not fail.
  - Fix: Fix the findings of the failed gate and push; the PR is decided again.
- **`merge-rule/approval-commit-valid`**: A Lectio-Approval commit must be signed by github-actions[bot] from a content-gates.yml run for this PR, with trailer head equal to its parent.
  - Fix: Drop the commit: only the merge-rule job writes approval commits. Approve with the label or /approve instead.
- **`merge-rule/review-block-approved`**: A review block is set to approved only with a configured reviewer’s approval or a valid approval commit.
  - Fix: Restore the pending review block; a reviewer approves with the label or /approve and the merge-rule job writes the block.
- **`merge-rule/approved-commit`**: A valid approval commit at the head means the PR was approved; nothing more is decided.
  - Fix: Nothing to fix.
- **`merge-rule/human-approval`**: A configured reviewer’s label or /approve comment after the last content commit approves the PR.
  - Fix: Ask a reviewer in config.reviewer.githubHandles to approve again after the last content commit.
- **`merge-rule/auto-merge`**: A PR auto-merges when every gate passes, both verifiers support every claim at autoMerge.minSupport and nothing is refuted.
  - Fix: Nothing to fix.
- **`merge-rule/protected-path`**: A PR that changes packages/gates/**, .github/** or config/** always needs a person (not configurable).
  - Fix: Ask a reviewer to approve, or split the content change from the code or config change.
- **`merge-rule/translation-needs-person`**: A PR that changes a translation (passages/i18n/**) always needs a person (not configurable): translations never auto-merge.
  - Fix: Ask a configured reviewer who reads the language to approve with the label or /approve.
- **`merge-rule/auto-merge-enabled`**: Auto-merge happens only while autoMerge.enabled is true.
  - Fix: Ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/deterministic-gates-ran`**: Every deterministic gate (schema, evidence, licence) must run before a PR can auto-merge.
  - Fix: Re-run the gates so each deterministic gate reports a result, or ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/verifiers-ran`**: The verifiers must run and report readable per-claim scores before a PR can auto-merge.
  - Fix: Re-run the gates with both verifier keys configured, or ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/every-claim-verified`**: The verifiers report a record for every claim of every changed passage.
  - Fix: Re-run the verifiers so they check every claim, or ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/live-verifiers`**: Verdicts from fake verifier clients (meta.fake) never auto-merge a PR.
  - Fix: Re-run the gates with live verifier clients (both keys configured), or ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/both-verifiers`**: With autoMerge.requireBothVerifiers, the confirmer and the refuter both give a verdict on every claim.
  - Fix: Re-run the verifiers, or ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/claim-support`**: Each verifier supports every claim at autoMerge.minSupport or higher.
  - Fix: Strengthen the claim’s sources or wording and push, or ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/verdict-supported`**: Each verifier’s verdict on every claim is "supported".
  - Fix: Fix the claim the verifier could not support and push, or ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/no-refutations`**: No more claims are refuted than autoMerge.maxRefutations allows.
  - Fix: Correct or remove the refuted claims and push, or ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/sensitive-claim`**: With autoMerge.sensitiveClaimsRequireReview, a claim flagged sensitive by the generator or either verifier needs a person.
  - Fix: Ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/no-flags`**: With autoMerge.flagsRequireReview, a gate flag needs a person.
  - Fix: Resolve the flagged findings and push, or ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/passages-only`**: With autoMerge.passagesOnly, only PRs that change nothing outside passages/ can auto-merge.
  - Fix: Ask a reviewer to approve, or split the passage change from the rest.
- **`merge-rule/same-repository`**: A PR from a fork always needs a person.
  - Fix: Ask a reviewer to approve.
- **`merge-rule/approval-counted`**: An approval counts only from a handle in config.reviewer.githubHandles, made after the last content commit.
  - Fix: Ask a configured reviewer to approve again after the last content commit.

### The runner (`runner`)

The runner reports these itself when a gate cannot be trusted to report.

- **`runner/gate-crashed`**: A gate must finish and report a result; it never throws.
  - Fix: Read the error in the message, fix the gate or the input that broke it, and re-run the gates.
- **`runner/invalid-result`**: A gate result must match the gate-result schema and carry the id of the gate that produced it.
  - Fix: Fix the gate so its result validates (`@lectio/schema/gate-result`): status and items must agree.
- **`runner/unknown-rule`**: Every finding must name a rule that its gate declares.
  - Fix: Declare the rule in the gate with defineRule, or correct the rule id in the finding.
- **`runner/report-missing`**: A gate job that ran hands its report to the merge rule; a missing report never counts as a pass.
  - Fix: Re-run the content gates; if the report is still missing, check that the job uploads it where the merge rule reads it.
- **`runner/regular-files`**: Every file a PR adds or changes is a regular file: symbolic links and submodules are refused, and no gate reads them.
  - Fix: Replace the link or submodule with the file itself, or remove it from the PR.

## Licence guard limitation

Every licence-gate run repeats this note (an `info` finding and `meta.limitation`); it comes from textguard (L-013):

> The index only detects overlap with World English Bible and Douay-Rheims wording. Copyrighted modern translations (NABRE, RSV-2CE, Jerusalem Bible) are caught only where they share runs with those texts; the quoted-run rule, the research prompt rules and human review are the remaining safeguards.

The quoted-run rule, the research prompt rules and the [reviewer](reviewer-guide.md) cover what the index cannot see.
Details: [licence gate README](../packages/gates/src/licence-gate/README.md).

## The gates comment

The merge-rule job keeps one sticky comment on the PR (hidden marker `<!-- lectio-gates -->`) and updates it on every
run. It has:

1. **The gates table**: one row per gate with Pass, Fail, Needs review or Skipped, and a count of findings.
2. **Findings**, grouped by file (whole-PR findings first) and then by claim, errors before warnings before notes.
   Each finding gives its severity, rule id, gate and JSON pointer, the message, then the rule and the fix.
3. A footer with the base, the head and the number of changed files.
4. **The merge rule's decision** and every reason for it.
5. `Checked head:` with the full commit sha, so a stale comment can be told from a current one.

This is the comment for an invented PR whose verifiers gave one claim low support and whose evidence rests partly on a
print source. It is rendered by the real merge rule and comment renderer, so it changes when they do:

```text
<!-- lectio-gates -->
## Lectio gates: needs review

| Gate | Status | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Schema tests (`schema`) | Pass | no findings |
| Evidence tests (`evidence`) | Needs review | 1 warning |
| Licence guard (`licence`) | Pass | 1 note |
| LLM verifiers (`verifiers`) | Needs review | 1 warning |

### Findings

#### Pull request

- **info** · `licence/pd-bible-overlap` (Licence guard): Limitation: The index only detects overlap with World English Bible and Douay-Rheims wording. Copyrighted modern translations (NABRE, RSV-2CE, Jerusalem Bible) are caught only where they share runs with those texts; the quoted-run rule, the research prompt rules and human review are the remaining safeguards.
  - Rule: No note text shares a run of licenceGuard.maxBibleRunWords or more words with a public-domain English Bible (World English Bible, Douay-Rheims).
  - Fix: Rewrite the sentence in your own words and point to the verse by reference instead of reproducing its wording.

#### `passages/MT.20.1-16.json`

**Claim `c2`**

- **warning** · `verifiers/claim-supported` (LLM verifiers) at `/claims/1`: c2 “The denarius was a usual day’s wage for a labourer.”: confirmer: supported 0.94; refuter: supported 0.78 (“the cited page gives the wage for soldiers, not labourers”)
  - Rule: Both verifiers judge every claim supported, with support at or above config.autoMerge.minSupport.
  - Fix: Cite a source (with an excerpt) that states the claim directly, or narrow the claim to what the sources say.

**Claim `c3`**

- **warning** · `evidence/print-source-flag` (Evidence tests) at `/sources/2`: source "s3" is a print source (a printed commentary, p. 112) and cannot be checked automatically
  - Rule: A claim resting on a print source cannot be checked automatically, so it is flagged for a reviewer.
  - Fix: A reviewer checks the citation against the book. Where possible, also cite a web or scripture source the gate can check.

<sub>Base `origin/main` · head `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567` · 1 changed file. Each finding names its rule; the fix says what to change.</sub>

### Merge rule: `needs-review` (waiting for human review)

- claim c2 (passages/MT.20.1-16.json): refuter support 0.78 is below 0.9
- the evidence gate flagged 1 finding
- the verifiers gate flagged 1 finding

Checked head: `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567` <!-- lectio-gates-head: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 -->
```

## Running the gates locally

```sh
npm run -w @lectio/gates gates -- run                    # all gates on origin/main...HEAD (committed changes only)
npm run -w @lectio/gates gates -- run --gates schema,licence --markdown out/comment.md
npm run -w @lectio/gates gates -- decide --results out/gates.json
npm run review:approve -- passages/<KEY>.json --reviewer <handle>
npm run gates:docs                                       # regenerate this file; --check only compares
```

Local runs are offline: the source fetcher is a fake (the log and the comment say so) and without `--llm live` and
the API keys the verifiers are skipped or run on fake clients, so a local `decide` never auto-merges.
